claims.claim: Residents pay a 5% final tax on dividends

sources.name: PwC: Greece, individual, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 08 September 2026. "Dividends are subject to a withholding tax (WHT) of 5%", which for individuals satisfies the full tax liability. claims.claim: The 7% Art. 5B regime needs a foreign pension

sources.name: PwC: Greece, individual, other tax credits and incentives
sources.says: Last reviewed 08 September 2026. Foreign pensioners who have not been Greek tax residents "for the previous five of the six years prior to the transfer" and who move from a state with an administrative cooperation agreement: "Every tax year, individuals will pay tax at a rate of 7% on their foreign-sourced income." Non-dom regime: the applicant must have "invested at least EUR 500,000 in real estate, businesses, or transferable securities or shares in legal entities based in Greece", pays EUR 100,000 a year, "for a maximum of 15 fiscal years"; for relatives added at EUR 20,000 a year each "the provisions of inheritance, gift, and parental grant tax will not apply."

sources.name: International Bar Association: preferential tax regimes for individuals moving their tax residency to Greece
sources.says: Dated 13 November 2024. Art. 5B: "the total foreign-source income of the individual is subject to an annual flat tax rate of seven per cent"; "the 5B regime covers a maximum of 15 tax years"; the applicant must receive a foreign pension and "must not have been a Greek tax resident for five out of the six years prior to the application". Art. 5A: "a lump sum annual tax of €100,000", an investment of "at least €500,000", "a maximum of 15 tax years"; "property located abroad is exempt from Greek inheritance and gift tax."

sources.name: Crowe Greece: alternative tax regimes
sources.says: Cites AADE decisions A.1147/2026 and A.1192/2026. Art. 5B: "Pensioners who move their tax residence to Greece" pay a "flat 7% tax" on "all their foreign-source income" "for up to 15 years"; "No Greek tax residence in 5 of the 6 years before the move". Art. 5A: a "flat annual tax of €100,000 on all their foreign-source income, whatever the amount", for up to 15 years, with "An investment of at least €500,000 in Greece"; "assets held abroad are exempt from Greek inheritance and gift tax."

"The minimum requirement is €3,500 per month for a single applicant", "increasing by 20% for a spouse and 15% for each dependent child"; qualifying income "such as pensions, rental income, dividends, or investments"; applicants "must have the correct health insurance"; "accommodation" is listed among the documents to prepare; holders must "spend at least 183 days each year in Greece"; "The FIP Visa does not allow employment or self-employment in Greece."

claims.note: Private insurance is stated plainly. Housing rests on one page listing "accommodation" among the documents; no page read says whether a lease or a deed is required, and the profiles do not say either.

claims.claim: The permit is renewable, needs 183+ days a year in Greece to renew, and allows no work

sources.name: Vardikos & Vardikos: Financially Independent Person visa
sources.says: Undated (footer 2026). "The minimum income requirement is set at 3.500 Euros per month." "This is increased by 20%, if the spouse is included in the application, and 15% for each child". Legal basis "Article 163 par.8 of the Greek Law (5038/2023)". "The residence permit is issued for 3 years and then it can be renewed." "There is a minimum stay requirement of 183 days per calendar year in Greece in order for the permit to be renewed." It "does not allow access to the labour market."

sources.name: TaxLaw (Iason Skouzos): residence permit for financially independent persons
sources.says: Posted 19 May 2025. Citing Ministerial Decision 225679/2024: "the minimum amount of three thousand five hundred (3,500) euros per month"; "this amount shall be increased by 20% for the spouse and 15% for each child". The permit runs three years, renewable; it needs "An insurance policy from a private insurance provider that fully covers his/her medical treatment and hospitalization"; it gives "no access to the labour market". Housing and minimum stay are not mentioned.

claims.note: Scores.visa stays 3 (workable but a high threshold).

claims.claim: The public ESY system is stretched, with long waits

sources.name: To Vima: Greek households shoulder heavy health costs, OECD report says
sources.says: Dated 15 November 2025, on the OECD's Health at a Glance 2025. "In 2024, 12.1% of Greeks said they had delayed or gone without needed medical care" (OECD average 3.4%); "Cost is the most common reason for postponing or skipping treatment, followed by long waits for public appointments"; "Nearly 39% of all health spending is paid directly out of pocket"; "many patients turn to private providers to avoid long waits or patchy availability".

claims.note: The OECD's own country note returned HTTP 403 (https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/country-health-profile-2025-country-notes_c0e8b8be-en/greece_9ca0bb52-en); a dated press report of the OECD figures was used.
